item.title: Combating the climate crisis to promote peace in Mali
item.description: Between 1970 and 2020, the country experienced at least 40 major climate shocks, with drought affecting around 400,000 people each year and reducing crop revenues by US$9.5 million annually, according to the World Bank.

item.title: Venezuela inflates release figures as political prisoners remain in limbo
item.description: As Venezuelan authorities claim a mass release of political prisoners, families wait outside detention centers without answers, or guarantees. Behind the government’s discourse of reconciliation, uncertainty and fear persist.

item.title: Truth-telling and treaty: Australian Indigenous lawyer’s commitment to real change for First Nations People
item.description: "For me, cultural continuity is both a responsibility and a source of strength. It reminds me of why this work matters and who it is ultimately for."

item.title: Beyond boubou and wax prints: Africa Fashion Tour changes perceptions of African creativity
item.description: African women’s wardrobes are diverse. Quite mixed, African fashion is sometimes traditional, sometimes Western, and sometimes a combination. It is unclassifiable when using a Western frame of reference.

item.title: After COP30, climate projects continue to threaten Indonesia’s Indigenous communities
item.description: "At COP30, countries rarely discussed the rights of indigenous peoples. Most progress for these groups took place outside the main talks."

item.title: Harassment and security threats forced the cancellation of a Pride-themed community event in Malaysia

item.title: How to turn Africa’s young demographic potential into a collective power
item.description: The African youth, an exploding population, needs support and programs to turn their potential into economic power.

item.title: Pakistan’s Aafia Siddiqui and the elusive truth in a landscape of politicized narratives
item.description: The Islamabad High Court repeatedly rebuked Pakistani officials for using the case of Aafia Siddiqui as a symbolic political tool rather than pursuing a sustained legal strategy.
